gaps.note: Cancelling the intermediate frames leaves D_{alpha_k} D_{alpha_0}^{-1}, not D_{alpha_k} D_{alpha_1}^{-1}. The stated right-hand side does not follow from the left, and the next paragraph uses the source frame, so the reader cannot check the identity as written.

gaps.quote: Undoing the exchange moves each output back to its input role, and multiplying by $\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign.
gaps.note: The page never says what undoing the exchange is (a reversed run of the network?) or what operator the undoing routes apply. The reader cannot check that undoing cancels the sign and leaves only the endpoint operators.

gaps.term: scratch roles are fixed with sign +1
gaps.quote: For a scratch role the construction has $\rho(w)=w$ with sign $+1$ (cited), so the undoing needs no correction there.
gaps.note: The claim that scratch roles map to themselves with sign +1 is only cited. The page does not say which construction this is or why it holds, and it is what makes the auxiliary values restored.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: This is the page's central conclusion about how the network computes its result and restores scratch values. It is only cited, and the page does not say what the round trip yields for a role or why it applies to scratch roles.
